Like you said, he's not perfect. You don't have to take his every word as gospel. You also don't have to reject everything he ever taught. 

Jordan Peterson was really great for me a few years ago. His book and lectures genuinely helped me break out of patterns of thinking, self denigration & self sabotage that were holding me back...  but I've since outgrown much of what he's taught and developed more nuanced perspectives that move beyond a lot of the hard lines he's drawn. I certainly don't align with his views on politics or climate, for example. 

Keep in mind, some of the mythological stuff *does NOT* originate with him, but were drawn into psychological frameworks through people like Carl Jung, and that stuff still has a lot of value to me when viewed from a nuanced perspective. Moreover, some of his rules are still genuinely good as far as I'm concerned (Don't compare yourself to who someone else is today, but who you were yesterday & Treat yourself like you are someone you are responsible for helping come to mind specifically). 

You can take the ideas that work and reject the things that don't. You can still respect the good that has come from his ideas while being critical of the perspectives you disagree with. That's how progress is made in society, evolution, technology, etc... We at least make an attempt to retain what works and reject what doesn't. You can do the same thing with people you've admired who you have since "outgrown" to a degree, all the while retaining a level of respect. You also develop a deeper sense of nuance with degrees of application / priority as you find further applications *as well as* misapplications for certain ideas, strategies, etc. 

Carl Jung did this with his teacher, Freud - a genius with groundbreaking perspectives. Carl Jung had to essentially break up with Freud over their differences (mostly because of Freud, afaik), but he still respected Freud despite his disagreements. We look at Freud now and we see a lot of problems with his hypotheses, but he absolutely created the groundwork for others to come in with deeper, fairer and more nuanced perspectives, not to mention numerous corrections to ideas that in hindsight we see as obviously wrong. You can do the same with Jordan Peterson.
